transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-06-17
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Carter, Marco Diaz (Redwood) — Priya Nair, Tom Reynolds, Aisha Khan, Ben Ortiz (Soluna)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Kickoff for procurement and security review for LLM inference vendor selection.
- Discussed MSA/DPA exceptions, KMS keying and VPC options (private vs hosted), pricing for Dedicated capacity, and a requested benchmark run for latency/cost.
- Agreed to share redline matrix, run benchmark, and reconvene after legal review.

Topics:
- Legal redlines (MSA/DPA) and audit evidence (SOC2/ISO)
- Private deployment options: VPC, on-prem, KMS/HSM integration
- SLA targets, rollback/fallback (hosted -> dedicated) and egress costing
- Pilot scope & benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Carter: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time, this is Lena from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Marco from our SE team is with me.  
[00:10] Priya Nair: Hi Lena, thanks. We, uh, quite a few people on our side — Aisha on legal, Tom infosec, Ben from platform — so we'll try to cover the lanes.  
[00:18] Marco Diaz: Morning/afternoon all. Quick agenda: legal redlines, deployment options (VPC vs hosted), k... k-m-s integration, and then Marco will propose a bench plan.  
[00:28] Aisha Khan: Great. We'll focus on DPA/MSA permissions, egress and data retention clauses. From legal side there are a couple of non-starters already flagged in the vendor intake doc.  
[00:36] Tom Reynolds: For InfoSec i'm mostly interested in keying (HSM/KMS), audit logs, and network isolation — we have to show separation for PII flows.  
[00:45] Lena Carter: Totally, understood. On the MSA side Redwood's standard is to keep data at rest encrypted, transit TLS 1.3, and we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration or optional HSM for Private deployments.  
[00:58] Ben Ortiz: For a Private deployment, do you mean full on-prem or VPC-hosted in our cloud account? We are leaning to VPC-hosted but with customer keys.  
[01:07] Marco Diaz: Yes, VPC-hosted is the typical approach — private control plane with customer-managed networking. You can bring your own KMS (BYOK) and we integrate via the standard KMS provider APIs; HSM is possible for on-prem or special enterprise pack.  
[01:24] Priya Nair: Pricing question — we'd like a sense of committed Dedicated cost vs pay-as-you-go hosted. Also need to estimate egress fees for model outputs.  
[01:32] Lena Carter: We can do both. For predictable throughput teams use Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) with monthly or annual commits; hosted is usage-based with lower commitment. Egress is billed as part of... well, depends on your cloud egress plus our outbound handling, we'll itemize that on the quote.  
[01:46] Tom Reynolds: One of our constraints: SOC2 + encryption at rest where Redwood doesn't have access to keys. Is that supported?  
[01:54] Marco Diaz: Yes: customer-managed keys — Redwood never sees the plaintext key; we fetch wrapped tokens from KMS per request if you deploy in Private/VPC. For hosted there's also a BYOK path but it has more operational steps.  
[02:10] Aisha Khan: On the DPA — we're going to request a retention cap where model session data is auto-deleted after 30 days; does Redwood support configurable retention windows?  
[02:18] Lena Carter: Yes, retention windows are configurable per-tenant and we can set default purge rules. There are caveats with caching (prefix/KV caching) that Marco can explain — sometimes caches are for performance and might require different handling.  
[02:32] Marco Diaz: Right, the runtime uses KV cache and prefix caching for latency. We can disable user-level caching for regulated flows, or we can encrypt cached blobs with your key. There are tradeoffs in latency/cost.  
[02:45] Ben Ortiz: Speaking of latency, what SLA numbers can we expect for a 8k context model and 40 concurrent sessions? We need p95 below 800ms for interactive features.  
[02:56] Marco Diaz: That target's ambitious for 8k with high concurrency — p95 around 600-900ms depends on model quantization and batching. With Dedicated GPUs pinned you can hit p95 ~700ms if we tune batching and use KV caching; without caching and on hosted it could slip.  
[03:16] Priya Nair: We need fallback plan if Dedicated is saturated — automatic fallback to compatible smaller model or to hosted, is that possible?  
[03:24] Lena Carter: Yes, smart routing and fallbacks are supported — you can route by latency or cost, and set automatic fallback to compatible model variants or another region. That's part of rollout policies.  
[03:34] Tom Reynolds: Any FedRAMP trajectory? We're not FedRAMP-bound immediately but may be in two years.  
[03:40] Lena Carter: We're tracking FedRAMP readiness; our compliance roadmap is public in the security pack but timeline varies. For now SOC2 Type II + ISO are our main evidence items; we can share audit artifacts under NDA.  
[03:54] Aisha Khan: On MSA redlines — we expect indemnity caps and specific data breach notifications within 48 hours. Can you commit to that window?  
[04:02] Lena Carter: We aim to notify customers promptly; the 48-hour window is reasonable for many of our enterprise agreements — legal will need to confirm exact language.  
[04:12] Priya Nair: How do we handle data residency? Some European lines must keep data in-region.  
[04:18] Marco Diaz: You can pin models/requests to region endpoints. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can provision in the EU region to satisfy residency constraints.  
[04:27] Ben Ortiz: For our pilot we want to run a true-to-prod load: 8k context, Nucleus-style prompts, 40 concurrent users, produce latency & cost CSV. Will Redwood run that benchmark within our VPC?  
[04:38] Marco Diaz: We can — suggested plan: we spin up a 2-hour Dedicated test in your VPC with 2-4 nodes matching the intended capacity, run a scripted workload and capture token cost and p95 latency. We'll need network access and sample prompts.  
[04:52] Priya Nair: Timeline? We want results before we commit in the approval lane.  
[04:57] Lena Carter: We'll target to have results in a week — Marco will run the bench and share raw outputs. We'll also deliver a short readout deck.  
[05:06] Aisha Khan: Please include the DPA redline matrix in the same packet so legal can review concurrently.  
[05:11] Lena Carter: Yep — i'll send the redline matrix and standard SOC2 artifacts under NDA.  
[05:17] Tom Reynolds: On encryption — do you support customer-managed HSM for signing and key rotation?  
[05:23] Marco Diaz: HSM is supported for Private on-prem installs and for select enterprise VPC customers through our HSM plug. Key rotation policies are compatible with standard KMS flows.  
[05:32] Priya Nair: One more commercial: if we commit 12 months, can we get a stepped discount and guaranteed burst capacity for 30% over baseline?  
[05:40] Lena Carter: Yes, we can structure committed pricing with burst allowances. I'll put options in the quote: monthly vs 12-month with burst, plus an option for reserved buffer capacity.  
[05:50] Ben Ortiz: Also want to confirm RBAC and audit trails — we need token-level logging to integrate with our SIEM.  
[05:56] Marco Diaz: Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tracing hooks; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM (S3/HTTP syslog) with the right retention settings.  
[06:08] Aisha Khan: Quick note: some vendor intake reviewers complained about broad subprocessor lists. We may ask for a narrow subprocessor list or acknowledgement of primary infra providers only.  
[06:18] Lena Carter: Understood — we'll provide a clearer subprocessors list and, where possible, offer carve-outs.  
[06:25] Priya Nair: Ok, actionable items and owners?  
[06:30] Lena Carter: Summarizing — Lena will send MSA/DPA redline matrix and security pack; Marco will run benchmark; Redwood to produce pricing options; Soluna to confirm approval lane and share network diags.  
[06:44] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Aisha will review redlines and flag any blockers.  
[06:49] Aisha Khan: I'll try to get back within three business days but i'll push for 48 hours on high-risk items.  
[06:55] Lena Carter: Great. We'll tentatively reconvene after results, say week of 2025-06-23?  
[07:02] Priya Nair: Week of 23rd works, we'll slot a 30-min readout.  
[07:08] Lena Carter: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and the bench schedule.  
[07:12] Tom Reynolds: Thanks.

End of transcript.
